title: Subaru CVT (2012-23 Impreza, Crosstrek, Forester, Legacy, Outback): shudder at takeoff or stopping, P2757 / P2762, updated valve body
summary: Subaru bulletin 16-156-25R: a redesigned CVT control valve body (stronger valve sleeve) fixes torque converter lock-up faults that cause P2757/P2762 and shudder when pulling away or coming to a stop. The bulletin gives a data-logging test to decide whether the valve body needs replacing.

specs.name: DTCs
specs.value: P2757 (torque converter clutch pressure control solenoid performance / stuck off), P2762 (lock-up duty solenoid); P06EF on 2014-16 Crosstrek Hybrid only

specs.name: Test
specs.value: From 25 mph to a stop, twice with CVT fluid below 104 °F and twice above 176 °F, logging all TCM data

specs.name: Replace valve body if
specs.value: Lock-up duty ratio differs by 10% or more between the hot and cold runs at the moment the converter clutch releases

specs.name: Graph range
specs.value: Torque converter speed and engine speed, 0-3000 rpm

specs.name: Labor
specs.value: 1.3 hr valve body replacement (B303-586); 0.5 hr electrical testing and diagnosis (C303-711)

steps.text: Symptoms: P2757 or P2762, shudder accelerating from a stop, or shudder decelerating to a stop. Crosstrek Hybrid can also set P06EF or fail to move after releasing the brake from an EV stop.
Diagnose any other DTCs first. If P2757 or P2762 is set, follow the service manual tree for it; if that ends in a valve body, replace it and do the torque converter relearn.
For a shudder with no codes: log a drive with the Subaru Select Monitor capturing all TCM PIDs. Slow from 25 mph to a full stop twice with CVT fluid under 104 °F, and twice more above 176 °F.
Graph engine speed and torque converter speed (0-3000 rpm). Find where the two lines split on each decel: that's the lock-up clutch releasing. Read the lock-up duty ratio there.
Subtract the cold-run duty ratio from the hot-run one (the bulletin's example: 40% - 23% = 17%). A difference of 10% or more means replace the valve body.
Finish with the torque converter relearn procedure, and repeat the relearn if the symptom isn't better.

body: Warranty claims require Subaru's CVT Diagnostic Assistance Application; for a non-warranty repair the manual data review above is an accepted path. The valve body replacement procedure itself is unchanged in the service manual.
